## Spectrum of AI Permissibility

Academic libraries translate broad campus academic integrity policies into concrete classroom and research behaviors. Across the corpus, institutions establish clear boundaries between permissible cognitive assistance and academic dishonesty.

```
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                    SPECTRUM OF AI PERMISSIBILITY                                   |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------+----------------------------------------+
| PROHIBITED USE           | CONDITIONAL / ASSISTIVE USE    | EXTENSIVE COLLABORATION                |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------+----------------------------------------+
| - Unacknowledged text/   | - Brainstorming search terms   | - Exploratory prompt iterations        |
|   code generation        | - Synthesizing notes/outlines  | - Comparative analysis of AI outputs   |
| - Submitting synthetic   | - Grammar and language editing | - Code generation with complete        |
|   prose as original work | - Search query optimization    |   attribution and methodology logs     |
| - Inputting PII or       | - Vendor tool summaries with   | - Advanced literature mapping and      |
|   unvetted research data |   source verification          |   thematic visualization               |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------+----------------------------------------+
```

---

## Core Institutional Policy Tiers

Academic library guides recommend three primary policy models for course syllabi:

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Tier 1: Prohibited Use
- **Definition**: Complete restriction on all GenAI tools.
- **Rationale**: Used in foundational courses to ensure mastery of baseline skills (e.g., introductory language acquisition, basic arithmetic, introductory prose composition).
- **Enforcement**: Submitting AI-generated content without explicit permission constitutes academic misconduct (e.g., UCSB, William & Mary Honor Code).

### Tier 2: Conditional Use with Explicit Disclosure
- **Definition**: Permitted for specific research and drafting phases (e.g., brainstorming, outlining, code debugging, language polish).
- **Requirement**: Mandatory inclusion of an **AI Disclosure Statement** documenting tools used, model versions, prompt text, and how outputs were adapted (William & Mary, UCSD, UC Irvine).

### Tier 3: Pervasive Integration
- **Definition**: AI tools are fully integrated into learning activities and assignments.
- **Pedagogy**: Focuses on advanced prompt engineering, comparative AI output auditing, and prompt log reflection.

:::

## Citation & Attribution Standards

All 11 institutions mandate attribution whenever GenAI tools contribute to academic work. The guides synthesize the official guidance from major style manuals:

| Citation Manual | Reference Entry Structure | In-Text & Methodology Disclosure |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **APA 7th Edition** | `Author: Company (e.g., OpenAI). Title: Model Name [Large language model]. URL.` | Provide description of prompt and excerpt in body text or append full chat transcript. Unique chat URLs should be provided where available. |
| **MLA 9th Edition** | `Title of Source: "Prompt text/description". Container: ChatGPT. Version: Date/Model. Publisher: Company. Date of Access. URL.` | Acknowledge in-text when paraphrasing AI output. AI should not be listed as an author in author field. |
| **Chicago Style** | Handled primarily via notes (footnotes/endnotes) rather than bibliography: include tool name, company, access date, and prompt description. | Include prompt details in footnote or parenthetical citation. Bibliography entry discouraged unless permalink exists. |
| **IEEE Style** | Treated as private communication or unpublished non-recoverable material. | Document model, company, date, and specific prompt details in text notes. |

::: {.callout-warning}
### AI Authorship Prohibition
Every surveyed library explicitly cites major academic publisher policies (Elsevier, Springer Nature, ACM, IEEE, PLOS, Taylor & Francis) stating that **GenAI cannot be listed as an author or co-author** on scholarly publications because non-human entities cannot take legal responsibility or intellectual accountability for manuscript integrity.
:::

---

## Data Privacy & Institutional Governance

Guides at **UC Merced**, **UC San Diego**, and **Chapman** emphasize institutional IT data classifications:
- **No PII or Sensitive Data in Public AI**: Users must never enter student records, patient data, confidential interview transcripts, or proprietary research into public tools.
- **Campus-Approved Secure Environments**: Only enterprise-licensed tools with zero-data-retention agreements (e.g., Microsoft Copilot via institutional SSO, ChatGPT Edu, ZotGPT) may process sensitive university workflows.
